title: Fulham sign Charles from Southampton for £30m
dek: Fulham completed the signing of midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton on a five-year contract. The 22-year-old, described as the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever, fills the midfield vacancy left by Sasa Lukic's departure to Ipswich and becomes the third major signing under new manager Alvaro Arbeloa.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Charles, 22, becomes the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever, signed on a five-year deal until June 2031 with an option to extend.
bottom_line: Charles's arrival completes Fulham's midfield reconstruction and signals sustained investment under Arbeloa. Watch whether the fee reflects immediate first-team impact or a longer development arc, with the Chelsea opener providing an early measure of readiness.
body: Fulham have completed the signing of midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton on a five-year contract, marking the club's third major addition under manager Alvaro Arbeloa since his arrival in early July.

Charles, 22, becomes the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer of all time, according to BBC Sport, surpassing the previous record held by Jamal Lewis, who joined Newcastle from Norwich for £15 million in 2020. The transfer fee was reported by BBC Sport as £26 million up front plus £4 million in add-ons, totaling £30 million, though ESPN reported the breakdown as £27 million plus £6 million in add-ons. The contract runs until June 2031, with an option for the club to extend for a further 12 months, per ESPN.

Charles has won 35 caps for Northern Ireland and brings experience across several English leagues. According to ESPN, he made his competitive debut for Manchester City in 2023 and spent one season there before joining Southampton, where he featured for three seasons. Most recently, he was on loan at Sheffield Wednesday during the 2024-25 season. Leeds United also showed interest in Charles during the transfer window, per BBC Sport.

The signing addresses Fulham's midfield need following Sasa Lukic's move to Ipswich Town for £9 million last week. Charles arrives as Fulham's third most expensive signing, behind striker Gonzalo Garcia (£34 million from Real Madrid) and winger Kevin (£34 million from Shakhtar), both acquired during Arbeloa's tenure, according to BBC Sport.

Arbeloa, the former interim Real Madrid manager during the second half of the 2024-25 season, has overseen a concentrated transfer push in his opening weeks. Alongside Charles, the club also signed Palacios from Real Madrid, per BBC Sport.
Fulham's Premier League campaign opens with a home fixture against Chelsea on Monday, 24 August.
